**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                               Date Issued: 17 December  2010</mark>** 



# ICSG Global Recyclables Survey 2010 Edition (covers 2008) 

The International Copper Study Group has released for sale its Global Recyclables Survey carried out in 2010 and covering information for the year 2008. The brief 9-page **2010 Annual Global Recyclables Survey** focuses on secondary refined production and copper content of directly melted copper and copper alloy scrap for the production of semis, casting ingots, castings, and, if available, other products such as powders, chemicals and plating anodes. 

The key **objective of the recyclables survey** is to increase the transparency and knowledge of supply and use of copper raw materials in the major continental regions of the world. The survey results also allow for assessing the historical development of the recycling rates (RIR) in particular countries and regions. The ICSG Copper Scrap Project, launched in 2007 and finished in 2010, has made valuable contributions to improving the Recyclables Survey report, in addition to improving ICSG information about and reporting on the global copper scrap market. 

**Information** for the recyclables survey includes reported data on copper scrap use from ICSG member and some non-member countries where such data is available from governmental or industry sources. These data are complemented with mass balance estimates of the Secretariat for those countries where survey data are not available. In addition to assessing total copper scrap use by country, the survey also aims to calculate the corresponding Recycling Input Rate. This rate measures the proportion of metal and metal products that are produced from scrap and other metal-bearing low grade residues. The RIR is mainly a statistical measurement for raw material availability and supply to a metal industry rather than an indicator of metal recycling efficiency of processes or products. 

This year the survey results indicated a 2.6% decrease of global copper scrap use following the small increase in global copper scrap use in 2007. In 2008, copper contained in total recyclables used amounted to over 2.8 million tonnes of secondary refined production (+3% year-on-year) and 5.4 million tonnes of direct melt (down 5% y-on-y). In terms of tonnage, secondary refined production increased by 80 kt-Cu and direct melt scrap use decreased by 295 kt-Cu. The decrease in direct melt usage in 2008 reflects in part falling overall semis production in major semis producing countries including the United States, Japan, Germany, Italy, Taiwan, the Korean Republic, France and others.
